title: Set up PyPI and the trusted publisher for squalor-slicer
lead:
S06 shipped the tag workflow and the `squalor-slicer` distribution name. Nobody
has a PyPI account step done yet: there is no project page, no trusted
publisher, and no GitHub `pypi` environment. PyPI was down when this was
filed, so the clicks wait. This slice is the procedure for the owner, who has
not used PyPI before.
findings_note: PyPI was down when S06 landed; account, GitHub environment, and pending publisher are still undone
boundary: **Not in this slice:** bumping the version, writing RELEASING.md, or pushing the release tag (S80). Do not create a PyPI API token. Do not start while status.python.org shows an outage.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Trusted publishing lets GitHub upload the package without an API token in the
repo. A pending publisher is what creates the PyPI project on the first
successful tag. It does not reserve the name `squalor-slicer` until that
upload. The name `slicer` on PyPI is already taken. The command and the import
stay `slicer`.

A published version number is permanent. PyPI will not accept the same version
again. Today `slicer.__version__` is `0.1.0`, so the only tag the workflow
will publish is `v0.1.0`. S80 owns the bump to 1.0.0 and the decision to cut
the tag. Do not tag from this slice.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml` — already on main; do not rewrite it
- `src/slicer/__init__.py` — `__version__` must equal the tag without the `v`
- GitHub environment `pypi` on `squalor-xyz/slicer`
- PyPI pending publisher for project `squalor-slicer`
- S80 — version bump, `RELEASING.md`, and the tag itself

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
No automated test. The procedure below is the whole check. Do not start it
while [status.python.org](https://status.python.org) shows a PyPI outage.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Do the account setup whenever PyPI is up. Push a tag only when the version in
the code is the one that should be public forever.

1. Create an account at https://pypi.org/account/register/ with an email you
   will keep. Open the confirmation link PyPI sends.

2. Two-factor authentication is required. In
   https://pypi.org/manage/account/ choose "Add 2FA with authentication
   application" and scan the QR code, or add a security key. Then choose
   "Generate recovery codes" and store them somewhere you can reach if you
   lose the phone. Without those codes, a lost authenticator can lock the
   project permanently.

3. On GitHub, open https://github.com/squalor-xyz/slicer/settings/environments
   and create an environment named exactly `pypi`. Add no secrets and no
   required reviewers. This needs admin on the repository. The workflow job
   refuses any other name.

4. While logged in to PyPI, open https://pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/
   and add a GitHub publisher:

   - PyPI project name: `squalor-slicer`
   - Owner: `squalor-xyz`
   - Repository name: `slicer`
   - Workflow name: `publish.yml`
   - Environment name: `pypi`

   Click Add. This is a pending publisher. It does not create the project and
   does not reserve the name. Do not create an API token. The workflow
   authenticates with GitHub's identity.

5. Leave the tag for S80 if the first public release should be 1.0.0. When
   the version in `src/slicer/__init__.py` is the one you want public, from a
   current `main`:

   ```sh
   git checkout main
   git pull
   git tag v0.1.0
   git push origin v0.1.0
   ```

   Use the real version in place of `0.1.0`. The tag must be `v` plus
   `__version__` with no other suffix. Pushing the tag is the publish. Watch
   the Publish workflow on the Actions tab.

6. When that workflow is green, https://pypi.org/project/squalor-slicer/
   exists and `pip install squalor-slicer` then `slicer --version` works.
   Later releases are a new version and a new tag. The publisher form is not
   filled in again.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- https://status.python.org is clear before you start.
- The GitHub environment `pypi` exists and has no secrets.
- PyPI's Publishing page lists a pending GitHub publisher with the five
  values above.
- No tag was pushed from this slice.
- After the real tag, the project page loads and a clean venv can install
  `squalor-slicer` and run `slicer --version`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One commit, filing this slice only. The PyPI and GitHub clicks are not a
commit. The release tag is not a commit in this slice.
